title: Maximum XOR After Operations
summary: Given an array of integers, perform any number of operations where each operation selects a non-negative integer x and an index i, then updates nums[i] to nums[i] AND (nums[i] XOR x).
statement: Given an array of integers, perform any number of operations where each operation selects a non-negative integer x and an index i, then updates nums[i] to nums[i] AND (nums[i] XOR x). The goal is to maximize the bitwise XOR of all elements in the array.
constraints: An operation may clear any chosen set bits of an array value but cannot create a bit absent from that value.
Apply any number of operations, then maximize the XOR of all values.
reference_solution:
def maximum_xor_after_operations(nums):
    answer=0
    for number in nums:answer|=number
    return answer
hints: If any input contains a bit, operations can retain it in exactly one value and clear it from the others.
OR all values to collect precisely the achievable set bits.
Every OR bit can be made odd in the final XOR, while no absent bit can be created, so OR is the maximum.
editorial: Every OR bit can be made odd in the final XOR, while no absent bit can be created, so OR is the maximum.

tests.explanation: The union of all set-bit positions is binary 111, so the maximum is seven.
Across the values, bits for one, two, and eight are available, producing eleven.
